question.worked_solution:
We can calculate $\frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{3x-5}$ using synthetic division.

For synthetic division to work, we need the coefficient of $x$ in the denominator to be equal to $1.$ So first, we factor the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{3x-5} & =\frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{3(x-\frac{5}{3})} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{(x-\frac{5}{3})}\end{aligned}
$$

Carrying out the synthetic division process on $\frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{(x-\frac{5}{3})}$, we arrive at the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{4} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{5}{3} & 9 & 12 & 0 & 0 & -25 \\  & ↓ & 15 & 45 & 75 & 125 \\  & 9 & 27 & 45 & 75 & 100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{(x-\frac{5}{3})} & =\frac{1}{3}(9{x}^{3}+27{x}^{2}+45x+75+\frac{100}{(x-\frac{5}{3})}) \\  & =3{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}+15x+25+\frac{100}{3x-5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our final result is

$$
\frac{9{x}^{4}+12{x}^{3}-25}{3x-5}=3{x}^{3}+9{x}^{2}+15x+25+\frac{100}{3x-5}.
$$
